topics.title: British Soldier’s Amputated Penis Following Skin Graft
topics.summary: A twenty-seven year old British soldier underwent a skin graft operation resulting in the amputation of his penis. After attempting suicide and experiencing personality changes, he was admitted due to an infected curved penis following the failed procedure; surgeons ultimately amputated it due to infection.

topics.title: Danny Bonadouche's Arrest and Transvestite Prostitute Incident
topics.summary: During a radio broadcast, hosts discussed Danny Bonadouche’s arrest following an incident involving a transvestite prostitute. Witnesses reported the alleged assault, theft of money, and subsequent attempts by Bonadouche to blame others while claiming police brutality.

topics.title: Radio Callers Discuss Sexual Anxieties
topics.summary: During a radio show discussion, callers share anxieties about their sexual experiences and desires, specifically regarding partner size discrepancies. One listener expresses disappointment with a man’s smaller endowment while another recounts an experience where he felt overwhelmed by the perceived ‘spectacularness’ of a larger male partner.

topics.title: Gary Lewis’ Vietnam Confessions
topics.summary: During an interview, Gary Lewis recounts his experiences as a ‘grunt’ in the Vietnam War, revealing he received little support from his father Jerry Lewis and that many people were unaware of their familial connection. topics.title: Gary Lewis Interview and Concert Promotion
topics.summary: Gary Lewis discusses his Vietnam service, family relationships with his father Jerry Lewis and brother, and his marriage. He promotes an upcoming concert featuring Gary Lewis and the Playboys with The Turtles at the Radisson Hotel in Melville, Long Island.

topics.title: Gary Lewis and the Playboys Interview
topics.summary: Gary Lewis discusses growing up in Beverly Hills around famous families, his father's involvement in his childhood activities, and his band's live performances. The interview includes discussion of Dean Martin, Frank Sinatra, and other Hollywood figures, followed by Bob Geldof performing "I Don't Care at All."
